title: David goal stands up as Canada beats Chile 1-0 in men's soccer friendly in Toronto
summary: The Canadian men's soccer team kicked off a new four-year cycle in style Saturday night with a 1-0 win over Chile in a chippy international friendly at BMO Field in Toronto.

image.caption: Canada's Jonathan David plays a pass during a 1-0 win over Chile in an international friendly at BMO Field in Toronto on Saturday night. (Chris Young/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Soccer·Recap
The Canadian men's soccer team kicked off a new four-year cycle in style Saturday night with a 1-0 win over Chile in a chippy international friendly at BMO Field in Toronto.
1st game for host side since falling to Morocco in World Cup Round of 16
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Sep 27, 2026 8:26 AM EDT | Last Updated: 20 minutes ago

It was the first game for the host side since falling to Morocco in the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup. Jonathan David scored the lone goal in front of a crowd of 23,310 and Dayne St. Clair earned the clean sheet.
"We wanted to come back here in Toronto after the World Cup to say thank you to the fans," said Canadian midfielder Mathieu Choiniere. "I think that's the best way that we did it - by a win."

The Canadian lineup was missing some key players for the first of three friendlies over the next fortnight. Captain Alphonso Davies (honeymoon), defender Derek Cornelius (hip) and goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau (personal) were unavailable.

David wore the captain's armband for 30th-ranked Canada. He was joined up top by Cyle Larin, who scored in the Canadian team's first World Cup game here on June 12, a 1-1 draw against Bosnia-Herzegovina.
Canadian men's soccer team defeats Chile in international friendly
"It felt amazing," Larin said. "I think I felt the same type of energy and we started off fast in the game and we were able to get one early.
"So it was amazing to be back and to get that feeling back at BMO."
The match billed as "The Homecoming" began with a ceremony to honour the World Cup squad, which qualified for the knockout stage for the first time and beat South Africa in the Round of 32.
Chile, the world No. 49, did not qualify for the World Cup. The South American country's last appearance in the tournament came in 2014.
Canada was on the front foot early and was rewarded when David tallied in the 12th minute.

Ralph Priso started the play with a long ball to winger Jacob Shaffelburg, who found Larin with a cross. Goalkeeper Christian Bravo stopped Larin's initial shot but the rebound floated across the goalmouth and David tapped it in with his left foot.
David raised a No. 13 Cornelius jersey in the air as he returned to the sideline. Cornelius was hurt during a training session earlier in the week.
"I'm always expecting to score every game," David said. "So I asked them for it to be prepared."

blocks.text: Chilean midfielder Lucas Cepeda was shown a red card in the 35th minute after getting tangled up with Canadian defender Richie Laryea.

As Cepeda was pulled down, his leg came upward and his boot caught Laryea on the side of the head. The contact drew blood near the eyebrow but Laryea stayed in the game after receiving medical attention.

Canada caught a break moments later when Niko Sigur was knocked down and St. Clair was caught out of the area. Chile's Jonathan Villagra had a chance to hit the ball into the empty net from distance but he put it over the bar.
Chile was down to nine men just four minutes into the second half.
Gabriel Suazo got the red after he was shown a second yellow card. His forearm caught Sigur in the head as they jumped for a ball.
Canada pressed with the two-man advantage but the Chilean backline held firm.
Jovan Ivanisevic made his national men's team debut as a wave of substitutes came on in the 62nd minute.
Hoilett makes final appearance
Junior Hoilett, in his final appearance with the squad, subbed in in the 76th minute. He was honoured for his 11-year run with the national team after the game.
"I was emotional, man," Hoilett said. "I was trying to hold it together when I first stepped on the field. It was a special moment."
A Laryea strike from distance in the 84th minute hit the post. Richard Chukwu made his national men's team debut in the 88th minute.
Head coach Jesse Marsch said Canada has set a long-term goal of reaching the top 24 in the world rankings as it looks to qualify for the 2030 World Cup in Portugal, Morocco and Spain.
Next up is an Oct. 3 friendly in Montreal against No. 50 Peru. Canada will visit the 16th-ranked United States on Oct. 6 in St. Paul, Minn.
